transcript: this musical is getting a lot of buzz right now in the New York theatre community and I don't think it quite lived up to the hype for me personally but I did still really enjoy it so Mexodus is a two person musical that makes use of live looping technology and it tells the story of a man who escapes sIavery in America by fleeing to Mexico and it focuses a lot on his relationship to a Mexican man who helps shelter him and through this story they're shedding light on this obscure facet of history where several thousand people did escape sIavery by fleeing to Mexico during that time but not many people know about it also explores some of the relationships between Black Americans and Mexicans both from a historical standpoint and also by making allusions to some of those dynamics as they exist today and all of that I found extremely compelling loved it and then with the live looping I went in a little bit skeptical partly because I remember with the musical Islander which also used a lot of live looping like I actually really loved Islander but I wasn't totally convinced that the show benefited from that format I kinda had this feeling of like “can we give these guys a budget” “and a full cast and a band?” and I was worried that I would feel the same way with this show but actually it ended up feeling very justified to me they managed to tie it into the themes and the concepts in a few clever ways including a beautiful Coup de Theatre at the end I should also mention that the talent and dexterity of these two performers is kind of ridiculous I mean just the sheer number of instruments that they both play very well in addition to the vocals it's kind of insane but as much as I like the concept and the themes and in some ways, the dynamic energy I feltsometimes like I was watching a show that was more geared towards children than adults which is fine you know, that's great I do actually think this show would be great for high schoolers but (a) that's not necessarily how it's marketed or framed and (b) I felt sometimes like they were maybe holding our hands through the messaging more than was needed rather than trusting us to understand the significance of what we were watching and I say this just because I think that held it back for me from being like the next big thing that I'm gonna rave about to everyone but clearly I'm in the minority here most people seem to really be loving this and I did still really appreciate the creativity and insight of the show and I would still recommend it to people if it sounds like it's up your alley
